messages:
Alex (Support): Hey team, Acme Ops reports ~50 users suddenly lost the 'product-admin' role after last night's SCIM sync. They say groups in Okta still exist. :confused:
Maria (CSM): Customer says it started after they enabled a new SAML attribute mapping (groups -> roles) in Okta. They didn't change any Redwood mappings.
Acme Ops: Yep — we added a SAML claim for group membership so downstream apps could read it. Rolled that out at 23:15 UTC. Deprovisioning kicked in at 23:20 and removed roles.
Alex (Support): Thanks. Can you confirm whether Okta is sending both SCIM group push and the SAML group claim for the same users? That smells like attribute precedence conflict.
Acme Ops: I pulled the logs. For user jdoe@example.com we saw a SAML JWT with groups: ["acme-prod-admins"] and a SCIM push for groups with externalId "okta:12345" and displayName "acme-prod-admins ". Note the trailing space.
Jordan (Eng): Trailing whitespace on SCIM displayName would cause mismatch against our group->role mapping (we match normalized displayName). If SAML claim uses clean name, and our deprovision path prioritizes group_lookups from claims over SCIM, we could end up removing role because the SCIM group wasn't recognized.
Li (SRE): Can we get the exact SCIM payload and the SCIM PATCH that applied? Also need the deprovision audit event.
Alex (Support): I captured two things from their logs: the SCIM membership PATCH and the deprovision event referencing role_id=prod-admin-42.
Alex (Support): SCIM PATCH (excerpt):
```
PATCH /scim/v2/Groups/okta:12345
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
  "Operations": [{
    "op":"replace",
    "path":"members",
    "value":[{"value":"00u1abcd","display":"jdoe@example.com"}]
  }]
}
```
Alex (Support): Deprovision event (audit): "user 00u1abcd removed from role prod-admin-42 via scim-group-iterator (source=group_display_normalized=\"acme-prod-admins\")"
Maria (CSM): So our normalization removed the trailing space, but the group lookup step earlier compared raw SCIM externalId string vs the mapping which expects externalId prefixed with "okta:" — here it matches, but the displayName mismatch caused a logic branch to prefer SAML claim resolution.
Jordan (Eng): Short diagnosis: two group sources (SAML claim and SCIM push) were reconciled in the wrong order. The SAML claim indicated user is not member (maybe claim was stale or scoped), SCIM push showed membership but with slight mismatch that triggered fallback logic which treated it as a removal.
Li (SRE): Repro steps request for eng: can we simulate with an Okta app configured to push both SCIM and SAML groups?
Jordan (Eng): I'll repro locally using a test Okta tenant. Steps I'm going to run: 1) create group 'acme-prod-admins ' (with trailing space) in Okta; 2) enable SCIM group push for that group; 3) add a user; 4) add a SAML group claim mapping that returns 'acme-prod-admins' (no trailing space); 5) remove the user from the SAML mapping (simulate claim change) while SCIM push still reports membership -> watch our reconcile job.
Alex (Support): Customer asked for quick mitigation now — any short-term fixes?
Jordan (Eng): Quick fixes: - Update Redwood group matcher to trim whitespace before normalization (safe). - Prefer SCIM group externalId precedence over SAML claims for deprovision decisions (config flag). Both are low-risk and can be rollout-caned.
Li (SRE): Also recommend adding a 5-minute grace window before hard deprovisioning roles when sources disagree (so transient rollout/claim race doesn't remove access).
Acme Ops: Do you need our Okta syslog or sample SAML JWTs? We can share.
Alex (Support): Please paste a sample SAML JWT and SCIM group payload (redact PII) to the thread. Jordan will start a patch. Maria, I'll follow up with the customer on the mitigation timeline.
OktaBot: Noted — last pushed group patch for Okta app 'Acme Redwood SCIM' at 2026-02-18T23:14:52Z.
Jordan (Eng): Patch plan: 1) trim displayName and externalId at ingestion (hotfix), 2) add config to prefer SCIM for group membership decisions (feature flag), 3) implement 300s deprovision grace window. I'll open PR and link here.
Jordan (Eng): Quick snippet I'm testing locally:
```py
# normalize group name
def normalize(name):
    return name.strip().lower()
```
Jordan (Eng): If we ship the normalization hotfix first, it should prevent mismatches from trailing whitespace. I'll target a canary deploy in prod tomorrow 06:00 UTC.
Maria (CSM): Acme Ops — will you permit a short maintenance canary window? They said yes for low-risk fixes.
Acme Ops: Yes, okay to canary. Please notify 15 min before.
Alex (Support): Thanks everyone. Action items: Jordan -> open PR and canary; Li -> monitor deprovision alerts for the canary window; Maria -> notify customer and schedule post-fix verification; Acme Ops -> upload redacted JWT + SCIM payloads.
Maria (CSM): Will do a post-deploy check with customer: verify previously removed users are not re-removed and roles can be reattached if needed.
Jordan (Eng): PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7891 (draft) — implements trimming + config flag. Will request review.
Li (SRE): I'll add a temporary alert rule to catch >=5 deprovisions/min for the prod-admin role during canary.
Acme Ops: Uploaded redacted payloads to the case. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Alex (Support): Closing loop once canary passes. :wave:
